title: no-weakened-confinement
description: >-
  cap_add SYS_ADMIN, SYS_MODULE, SYS_RAWIO or DAC_READ_SEARCH, and security_opt seccomp:unconfined, apparmor:unconfined, label:disable or systempaths=unconfined, weaken Compose container isolation. What each setting removes.
---

Docker starts a container with a short list of Linux capabilities, a seccomp filter that blocks dangerous syscalls, an AppArmor or SELinux profile, and masked paths under `/proc` and `/sys`. Each of those is a layer between a compromised process and the host kernel. `cap_add` and `security_opt` are how a Compose file removes them, and they are often added to get past one error and never taken out. This rule reports:

- **`cap_add`** entries for `SYS_ADMIN`, `SYS_MODULE`, `SYS_RAWIO` and `DAC_READ_SEARCH`, in any case and with or without the `CAP_` prefix.
- **`security_opt`** entries `seccomp:unconfined`, `apparmor:unconfined`, `label:disable` and `systempaths=unconfined`, written with either `:` or `=`.

`SYS_ADMIN` covers mounts and a large part of the kernel's interface. `SYS_MODULE` loads code into the host kernel. `SYS_RAWIO` reaches raw I/O ports and memory. `DAC_READ_SEARCH` bypasses file read checks, and with it a container can open host files by handle. `cap_add: [ALL]` is reported by [no-privileged-service](/docs/reference/rules/no-privileged-service) as an error.

`NET_ADMIN`, `NET_RAW` and `SYS_PTRACE` are not reported, because VPN clients and monitoring tools need them.

## What the rule catches

```yaml title="compose.yaml — a broad capability and no syscall filter"
services:
  agent:
    image: my-agent:1.2.0
    cap_add:
      - SYS_ADMIN
    security_opt:
      - seccomp:unconfined
```

Scanning this file reports:

```text
⚠ WARN [docker-doctor/no-weakened-confinement]
  Service 'agent' sets cap_add 'SYS_ADMIN', which lets it mount filesystems and reach most of the kernel.
```

## Why it matters

A container shares the host's kernel, so the capabilities, syscall filter and security profile are the only things that limit what a compromised process can ask of it. Removing them widens the kernel surface it can attack and turns an ordinary bug into a host compromise. The runc escapes [CVE-2025-31133](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/security/advisories/GHSA-9493-h29p-rfm2) and [CVE-2025-52565](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/security/advisories/GHSA-qw9x-cqr3-wc7r) show how much rides on these defaults. Their advisories say not to run untrusted images, and for containers without user namespaces to avoid root privileges and turn on no new privileges. A service that adds `SYS_ADMIN` or sets `seccomp:unconfined` works against that advice.

## How to fix it

Remove the capability or the `security_opt` entry. If the service needs one specific thing, grant that instead, such as a single device in `devices`.

```yaml title="compose.yaml — one narrow capability, privilege gain blocked"
services:
  agent:
    image: my-agent:1.2.0
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
```

Start from no extra access and add only what the error asks for:

- **A device**: list it in `devices` instead of adding a capability.
- **A mount**: use a volume, or a `tmpfs`, instead of `SYS_ADMIN`.
- **A blocked syscall**: write a seccomp profile that allows that syscall and point `security_opt` at it with `seccomp:./profile.json`. The rule does not report a custom profile.
- **Privilege gain**: add `no-new-privileges:true` to `security_opt`.

Some low-level tools, such as profilers and sandboxes that run their own containers, ask for these settings. Set this rule to `off` in `docker-doctor.config.json` for a project that exists to run such a tool.

## Rule details

- **Rule key** — `docker-doctor/no-weakened-confinement`
- **Category** — Compose
- **Default severity** — `warning`
- **Applies to** — Docker Compose files

Explain this rule from the CLI:

```bash
npx @docker-doctor/cli@latest rules explain docker-doctor/no-weakened-confinement
```

Change its severity — or turn it off — in your [config file](/docs/reference/configuration):

```ts
// docker-doctor.config.ts
export default {
  rules: {
    "docker-doctor/no-weakened-confinement": "off",
  },
};
```

Severity affects the [health score](/docs/reference/scoring): `error` findings cost more points than `warning`, and `info` costs the least.
